ei.title: Evolution and Continuity of Fictional Characters
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: In most fiction, characters' lives are limited to the individual work. Readers may disagree on the characteristics and traits of fictional figures, and in drama there is room for different interpretations of characters. However, it is less common for characters in literary fiction to reappear in subsequent works than in genre fiction, where series featuring the same central characters are common. This is even more pronounced in comics, which are typically serialized in newspaper strips or comic books. Thus characters introduced in the 1930s, like Superman and Batman, may still enjoy new adventures decades later. During these characters' long histories, they change in various ways for a variety of reasons. If a character is created by a single author, like Sherlock Holmes, the character's core traits may change little from story to story, but readers learn more about him with each successive story. On the other hand, if characters are the work of several hands over decades, they may change considerably.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① limited=제한된(수동태 정상), ② featuring=~을 특징으로 하는(현재분사 정상), ③ serialized→serialize 오류(be+p.p. 수동태 필요), ④ introduced=소개된(과거분사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① limited: 'characters' lives are limited to the individual work' — be+p.p. 수동태 정상

❌ ② featuring: 'series featuring the same central characters' — 현재분사로 series 수식, 능동의 의미 정상

✅ ③ serialize: 'which are typically serialize in newspaper strips' — be동사 뒤 수동태가 필요하므로 serialized(과거분사)가 와야 함. 원형 serialize는 수동태 불가 ← 정답

❌ ④ introduced: 'characters introduced in the 1930s' — 과거분사 후치수식 정상
det.tip: be동사 + p.p. 수동태 구조: are serialized(연재되다). 원형 serialize는 be 뒤에 올 수 없음

det.korean: ① are 오류(주어 This는 단수이므로 is → are로 바뀐 것이 틀림), ② pronounced=확연한(형용사 정상), ③ enjoy=즐기다(조동사 뒤 원형 정상), ④ successive=연속적인(형용사 정상)

✅ ① are: 'This are even more pronounced' — 주어 This는 단수 대명사이므로 is가 맞음. are(복수)는 수일치 오류 ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① limited=제한된(적절), ② common→uncommon 오류(장르 소설에서 시리즈는 흔함), ③ enjoy=즐기다(적절), ④ considerably=상당히(적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① limited: '등장인물의 삶이 개별 작품에 제한된다'는 문맥에 적절

❌ ③ enjoy: '슈퍼맨과 배트맨이 수십 년 뒤에도 새로운 모험을 즐긴다'는 자연스러움

det.korean: ① interpretations=해석(적절), ② pronounced=확연한(적절), ③ core→marginal 오류(핵심 특성이 맞음), ④ successive=연속적인(적절)

❌ ① interpretations: '드라마에서 등장인물에 대한 다양한 해석의 여지가 있다'는 문맥 적절

❌ ② pronounced: '만화에서 이 현상이 더 확연하다'는 문맥 적절

❌ ④ successive: '연속되는 각 이야기마다 더 많이 알게 된다'는 문맥 적절

Readers may disagree on the characteristics and traits of fictional figures, and in drama there is room for different interpretations of characters. However, it is less common for characters in literary fiction to reappear in subsequent works than in genre fiction, where series featuring the same central characters are common. This is even more pronounced in comics, which are typically serialized in newspaper strips or comic books. Thus characters introduced in the 1930s, like Superman and Batman, may still enjoy new adventures decades later. During these characters' long histories, they change in various ways for a variety of reasons. If a character is created by a single author, like Sherlock Holmes, the character's core traits may change little from story to story, but readers learn more about him with each successive story. On the other hand, if characters are the work of several hands over decades, they may change considerably.
